I'm an old fart and I like Jeff Cooper, but perhaps not for the reasons you might think. He saw things very differently than I do and I often disagreed with him, but he was also right, surprisingly right, about a lot of things. In my mind this is exactly the sort of author I want to read. I grudging accepted a lot of his views and I'm the better for it, I think. He's entertaining to read and he gets right to the point, traits I also value highly.

The Art Of The Rifle is a fine book about rifle craft. It is expensive though. Principles of Personal Defense is affordable, short and easy to read, and while it does not go into detail about firearms, in discusses is plain clear language the mental and moral principles of using firearms defensively. If this sphere of firearms use is of interest to you, this is a must-read. Massad Ayoob is another old-school defensive guru worth reading.

The Modern Technique Of The Pistol was not written by Cooper but it describes his approach to pistol craft in detail. It is dated now, and once again it is a stupidly expensive book, but it what most current pistol doctrine is based on, so you should grab a copy if you have a chance.

If you're into technical stuff like rifle accuracy, visit a benchrest forum and read what they are reading. Nobody know real accuracy like the guys who compete off of sandbags. Keep in mind the guys deal with extremes and it is not always practical to follow their ways with regular firearms use.
